title: Κολοιὸς καὶ ὄρνεα
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 162. Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ζεὺς βουλόμενος βασιλέα ὀρνέων καταστῆσαι, προθεσμίαν αὐτοῖς ἔταξεν ἐν ᾗ παραγενήσονται πάντα, ὅπως τὸν ὡραιότατον πάντων καταστήσῃ ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς βασιλέα.
sentences.tr: Zeus boulomenos basilea orneōn katastēsai, prothesmian autois etaxen en hēi paragenēsontai panta, hopōs ton hōraiotaton pantōn katastēsēi ep’ autois basilea.
sentences.l: Zeus, wishing to set up a king of the birds, appointed for them a day on which they should all present themselves, so that he might set the fairest of all over them as king.
sentences.i: Zeus wanted to appoint a king over the birds, and set them a day on which they were all to present themselves, so that he might make the fairest of them their king.
sentences.n: προθεσμία is a day fixed in advance, a term out of Athenian law, and Zeus here runs his business by Athenian procedure throughout. ὅπως with the subjunctive gives the purpose. ὡραῖος is 'in season, at its bloom', and so of a creature at its handsomest. The relative clause takes the future indicative παραγενήσονται where a subjunctive might be looked for — the day is simply stated as the day they will come.

sentences.t: Τὰ δὲ παραγενόμενα ἐπί τινα ποταμὸν ἀπενίζοντο.
sentences.tr: Ta de paragenomena epi tina potamon apenizonto.
sentences.l: And they, having presented themselves, were washing themselves at a certain river.
sentences.n: τὰ ὄρνεα is neuter plural, and Greek ordinarily gives a neuter plural subject a singular verb; here, and again at ἦλθον πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα below, the verb is plural. Chambry prints it so; the looser agreement is ordinary in later Greek. ἀπονίζομαι in the middle is to wash oneself clean, and the imperfect ἀπενίζοντο leaves them at it. ἐπί with the accusative is motion towards, compressed into the verb of washing: they went to the river and washed there.

sentences.t: Κολοιὸς δέ, συνιδὼν ἑαυτὸν δυσμορφίᾳ περικείμενον, ἀπελθὼν καὶ τὰ ἀποπίπτοντα τῶν ὀρνέων πτερὰ συλλεξάμενος, ἑαυτῷ περιέθηκε καὶ προσεκόλλησε.
sentences.tr: Koloios de, synidōn heauton dysmorphiāi perikeimenon, apelthōn kai ta apopiptonta tōn orneōn ptera syllexamenos, heautōi periethēke kai prosekollēse.
sentences.l: But a jackdaw, having seen himself wrapped about with ill-shapedness, having gone off and having gathered up the feathers falling from the birds, put them round himself and glued them on.
sentences.i: But a jackdaw, seeing how ill-favoured he was, went off, gathered up the feathers the birds were shedding, fitted them about himself and stuck them on.
sentences.n: περίκειμαι is 'lie round about'; the thing worn normally stands in the accusative, and the dative δυσμορφίᾳ here is the looser use — ill-shapedness lies about him like a garment he did not choose. συνοράω is to see a thing whole, to take it in at once. Three aorist participles and then a pair of main verbs — the ordinary engine of these fables, one participle per step and the finite verbs for the outcome.

sentences.t: Συνέβη οὖν ἐκ τούτου εὐειδέστερον πάντων γεγονέναι.
sentences.tr: Synebē oun ek toutou eueidesteron pantōn gegonenai.
sentences.l: It came about, therefore, from this that he had become better-looking than all of them.
sentences.n: γεγονέναι is a perfect infinitive: not that he became so at a moment, but that he now stood so. εὐειδέστερον is a comparative with πάντων as its genitive of comparison.

sentences.t: Ἐπέστη οὖν ἡ ἡμέρα τῆς προθεσμίας καὶ ἦλθον πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα πρὸς τὸν Δία.
sentences.tr: Epestē oun hē hēmera tēs prothesmias kai ēlthon panta ta ornea pros ton Dia.
sentences.l: So the day of the appointed term arrived, and all the birds came to Zeus.
sentences.n: ἐπέστη is literally 'stood over', the regular verb for a day or an hour coming upon one — the same word used of a god or a dream appearing at a man's side; English has no verb that keeps both the standing and the arriving, and 'arrived' takes the sense. ἡ ἡμέρα τῆς προθεσμίας is the day of the term set in the first sentence.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ κολοιὸς ποικίλος γενόμενος ἧκε καὶ αὐτός.
sentences.tr: Ho de koloios poikilos genomenos hēke kai autos.
sentences.l: And the jackdaw, having become many-coloured, came himself too.
sentences.n: ποικίλος is 'dappled, of many colours', and it is also the standing Greek word for a character that is not of one piece — a bird that is now literally ποικίλος and was always so in the other sense.

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ Διὸς μέλλοντος χειροτονῆσαι αὐτοῖς τὸν κολοιὸν βασιλέα διὰ τὴν εὐπρέπειαν, ἀγανακτήσαντα τὰ ὄρνεα, ἕκαστον τὸ ἴδιον αὐτοῦ πτερὸν ἀφείλετο.
sentences.tr: Tou de Dios mellontos cheirotonēsai autois ton koloion basilea dia tēn euprepeian, aganaktēsanta ta ornea, hekaston to idion autou pteron apheileto.
sentences.l: But Zeus being about to elect the jackdaw king for them because of his fine appearance, the birds having grown indignant, each took away from him its own feather.
sentences.i: But when Zeus was on the point of voting the jackdaw their king for his fine looks, the birds took it ill, and each pulled off its own feather.
sentences.n: τοῦ Διὸς μέλλοντος is a genitive absolute. χειροτονέω is to elect by a show of hands, the Athenian assembly's own word; here Zeus is its subject, so the god does alone what a citizen body would do together. The sentence changes footing halfway — ἀγανακτήσαντα, an aorist participle, agrees with τὰ ὄρνεα, but the verb ἀφείλετο is singular, taking ἕκαστον, 'each one', for its subject; the plural crowd resolves into one bird at a time.

sentences.t: Οὕτω τε συνέβη αὐτῷ ἀπογυμνωθέντι κολοιὸν πάλιν γενέσθαι.
sentences.tr: Houtō te synebē autōi apogymnōthenti koloion palin genesthai.
sentences.l: And so it came about for him, stripped bare, to become a jackdaw again.
sentences.n: The story ends where it began, on the word it began with: κολοιὸν πάλιν γενέσθαι, to be a jackdaw over again. ἀπογυμνόω is to strip a thing quite bare.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἱ χρεωφειλέται, μέχρι μὲν τὰ ἀλλότρια ἔχουσι χρήματα, δοκοῦσί τινες εἶναι, ἐπειδὰν δὲ αὐτὰ ἀποδώσωσιν, ὁποῖοι ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἦσαν εὑρίσκονται.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn anthrōpōn hoi chreōpheiletai, mechri men ta allotria echousi chrēmata, dokousi tines einai, epeidan de auta apodōsōsin, hopoioi ex archēs ēsan heuriskontai.
sentences.l: So too the debtors among men, so long as they hold other people's money, seem to be somebodies, but when they have given it back, they are found such as they were from the beginning.
sentences.n: τινες εἶναι, 'to be some persons', is Greek for being somebody of consequence — the indefinite pronoun does the whole work, and there is no adjective to help it. μέχρι μέν with the indicative against ἐπειδάν with the subjunctive holds the time they keep the money apart from the moment they hand it over. εὑρίσκονται is passive: they are found out to be.
